metadata.title: Nvidia reportedly approaches Arm CEO Rene Haas in search for Jensen Huang successor

content.text:
Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD) has reportedly approached Arm Holdings chief executive Rene Haas as a potential successor to Jensen Huang, as the artificial intelligence (AI) chipmaker searches for permanent leadership following the former chief executive's departure.
Recruitment firm Heidrick & Struggles, appointed by Nvidia's board to oversee the search, has contacted Haas about the position, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday, quoting a person familiar with the matter.
The firm has also begun approaching other executives who could be considered for the role, according to the report.
Haas has led Arm since 2022, overseeing its expansion as demand for the British chip designer's processor architectures grows across data centers, smartphones and artificial intelligence applications.
He previously spent seven years at Nvidia, rising to vice-president and general manager of its computing products business before joining Arm in 2013.
His familiarity with Nvidia's operations and experience leading a publicly traded semiconductor company could make him a potential candidate, although the approach does not mean he has agreed to pursue the position.
Finance chief Colette Kress is serving as interim chief executive of Nvidia while the board considers candidates.
The leadership search comes at a critical time for Nvidia, which has become one of the world's most valuable companies amid surging demand for its AI processors.
A change at the top could influence the company's strategic direction as it navigates intensifying competition, export restrictions and growing scrutiny of its business in China.
